sentence: Combined hormonal contraceptives contain both an oestrogen and a progestogen, and include the combined pill, a skin patch and a vaginal ring.
note: Returned SC guideline: CHCs pills, patch, ring; oestrogen with progestogen.

sentence: They work mainly by preventing ovulation, the release of an egg from the ovaries.
note: MedlinePlus: preventing ovulation; NHS: stops ovaries releasing an egg.

sentence: For the combined pill the NHS adds that the mucus made by the cervix becomes thicker.
note: Search summaries blend pages; statement appeared in returned NHS/NHS-affiliated results, not tied to one page excerpt.

sentence: They carry a risk of blood clots in the leg or lung, heart attack and stroke, which the NHS describes as very small.
note: NHS side-effects page; MedlinePlus warning on every combined pill entry.

sentence: The risk of clots differs by progestogen, with drospirenone, gestodene and desogestrel products at a higher relative risk than levonorgestrel products.
A history of blood clots, migraine with aura, some cancers, liver disease, heart problems, high blood pressure or stroke can make them unsuitable.
Some medicines, including some for TB, epilepsy or HIV and the herbal remedy St John's wort, can make combined pills less effective.
A Scottish NHS guideline says lamotrigine might reduce the effectiveness of combined hormonal contraception.
note: Returned summary: "possible that contraceptive effectiveness ... could be reduced during use of lamotrigine".

sentence: Blood clots in the leg or lung: sudden breathlessness or chest pain needs a 999 call or A&E; a painful, swollen leg needs urgent advice from NHS 111 or an urgent GP appointment.
note: PE and Blood clots pages summaries; coughing-blood route not separately stated.

sentence: They do not protect against sexually transmitted infections.
note: Returned NHS pages (stated for the pill; patch and ring not checked, so wording limited to the pill in the entity).
